long_biography.plain_text:
Carpets gave Simon Reuben his first commercial foothold. He imported them, acquired a carpet manufacturer and used the proceeds to buy property. His brother David, by contrast, developed experience in metals trading. They later combined their businesses in Transworld. Its aluminium trading and production interests became the principal engine of their first large fortune.

After selling their principal metals interests, the brothers shifted the shared capital into property and a wider investment portfolio. Their family office now spans real estate development, private equity, technology, data centres and other asset-backed businesses. Simon is therefore best understood as a co-builder and current family-office principal. His early property work and participation in Transworld are personal career facts. The major holdings and later investment results belong to the brothers' jointly managed enterprise, not to Simon alone.

uncertainties: Public reporting often treats David and Simon Reuben as a unit. The dossier attributes only Simon's carpet, carpet-company and early property work to him individually; Transworld, later property holdings, technology investments and the wider portfolio are attributed jointly to the brothers or their family office.

David Reuben entered metals trading before Simon joined him. Metals & Mining is nevertheless the wealth-creation classification for Simon because the jointly operated Transworld metals business is consistently identified as the engine of the brothers' first large shared fortune; David's earlier personal metals career is not attributed to Simon.

The current portfolio includes substantial real estate, but current Forbes and company material also document technology, private equity, venture capital, data centres, resources and other investments. Diversified is therefore used instead of assuming property alone still dominates the shared fortune.

Some low-quality biographical pages report Simon's birth year as 1944. The identity-verified Companies House record gives May 1941 and the current Forbes age is consistent with 1941, so May and 1941 are proposed while the unpublicised birth day remains blank.

Birth in Mumbai is strongly supported, but birth there does not establish Indian citizenship. No reliable evidence for a current second nationality was found, so secondary nationality remains unproposed.

The current Companies House record establishes a Reuben Foundation directorship but does not by itself quantify Simon's individual role in each grant. Philanthropic achievements are therefore not used to classify or expand the biography.

No identity-verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website was found. The existing joint Wikipedia record is retained; the exact Forbes profile and official company website are proposed separately.

Current net-worth estimates, rankings, asset values, ownership percentages, private-family trivia, allegations, legal matters, controversy, politics and vessel material are excluded from the biographies.
